result.title: Steering Automated Scientific Discovery via Audited Epistemic Exploration
result.summary: Scientific discovery requires revisiting the hypotheses in light of new evidence and identifying promising directions beyond those already explored. However, research agents often make claims that are not supported by their observations, explore a narrow hypothesis space, and retain beliefs despite recognizing conflicting evidence. These failures motivate the search for an explicit epistemic state that captures both beliefs about existing hypotheses and directions for further exploration. To this end, we propose Epistemic Compass (EpiCompass), a plug-and-play scaffold that maintains this state through an epistemic tree linking hypotheses, evidence, beliefs, and revisions. As an investigation progresses, EpiCompass reassesses the hypotheses explored against accumulated evidence and uses unresolved conflicts and unexplored directions to guide hypothesis generation. It selects candidates by anticipated epistemic gain, accounting for both refinement of existing hypotheses and expansion of the hypothesis space, and verifies the final conclusion against the accumulated evidence. Experimental results across three scientific discovery benchmarks and three LLM backbones demonstrate that EpiCompass consistently outperforms baselines, with further analyses showing reductions in errors of unsupported claims and failures to revise beliefs.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EpiCompass 即插即用框架，用链接假设、证据、信念与修订的「认知树」显式维护 epistemic state，按预期认知增益选择候选假设并对照累积证据核验最终结论，在三个科学发现基准与三个 LLM 骨干上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其显式信念状态、冲突驱动的假设重访与「预期认知增益」候选选择，可能为 LVR 中 STOP 决策、视觉证据筛选与状态更新提供概念参照，需核查这些机制能否对应到 latent 推理状态的维护与读取。
